events.headline: Houthi Missile Strike on Riyadh Airport Kills 12-13, Wounds 300+, Deadliest Saudi Attack in a Decade
events.summary: A Houthi missile strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on October 10, 2026, killed 12-13 people and wounded over 300, including foreign nationals from Bangladesh, the US, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan. It was the third Houthi strike on the airport within a week, following strikes that destroyed a Saudia A320; the airport remains closed under an extended NOTAM through at least October 17.

events.headline: Roof Collapse at Peshawar School Kills at Least 27-32 Children and a Teacher
events.summary: The roof of a two-story building at Al Khair Public School in Peshawar collapsed on the morning of October 15, 2026, after heavy overnight rain destabilized the structure. The death toll stands at 27-32 children plus one teacher, with about 50 injured; the school owner has been arrested and an investigation launched.

events.headline: France Unrest Enters Fourth Week: Up to 800,000 Protest, Limoges Town Hall Burned, 6,100 Detained Since Oct 1
events.summary: An estimated 550,000-800,000 people protested nationwide on October 17 over cost-of-living pressures; Limoges's 143-year-old town hall was set ablaze and Lyon's tourist office torched. The Justice Ministry says 6,100 people have been taken into custody since unrest began October 1, with 1,200 detained and 150 police injured on October 17 alone.

events.headline: DRC Ebola Outbreak Toll Climbs to 9,277 Cases, 4,478 Deaths as Kenya Confirms Second Case
events.summary: As of October 14, the DR Congo Ebola outbreak has reached 9,277 confirmed cases and 4,478 deaths, making it the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record. Kenya confirmed a second case the same day in a quarantined contact of its first patient, who is now in treatment.

events.headline: Gaza Ceasefire 'In Name Only' One Year On, Over 100 NGOs Say, as Death Toll Holds at 1,493
events.summary: More than 100 NGOs say Gaza's ceasefire 'exists in name only' as the confirmed death toll under the truce stands at 1,493 killed and 5,299 wounded. The UN's human rights office separately verified only 1,076 conflict-related deaths through July using stricter methodology, highlighting discrepancies in casualty counting.

events.headline: Russia Strikes 15+ Power Facilities Across Ukraine, Killing Seven, as Zaporizhstal Hit Fifth Time
events.summary: Russia struck more than 15 power facilities across 10 Ukrainian regions on October 17, killing 7 and injuring about 90. The Zaporizhstal steelworks was hit with six ballistic missiles in its fifth such attack, and rolling blackouts hit Odesa before power was restored to over 500,000 consumers.

events.headline: Eritrean Troops Reported Inside Ethiopia's Tigray Region, Raising Fears of Renewed War
events.summary: Witnesses reported Eritrean troop convoys moving from the border town of Zalambessa through Adigrat into central Tigray between late September and early October. Ethiopia calls it an invasion while Eritrea denies the deployment and accuses Ethiopia of threatening its ports, marking a major escalation beyond the two countries' severed diplomatic ties.

events.headline: Four Firefighters Killed Battling Blaze at Indonesia's Bromo Tengger Semeru Park Amid Worst Fire Season in a Decade
events.summary: Four people, including two park officers and two volunteers, were killed October 15 fighting a wildfire at Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park after being trapped by shifting winds and smoke; two others were hospitalized with severe burns. Indonesia is experiencing its worst fire season in over a decade, with haze ongoing since August 11 and over 2,020 flights affected regionally.
events.locationName: Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park, East Java, Indonesia

events.headline: Houthis Strike Yemen's Presidential Palace in Aden, Killing Five; Missiles Land Near Airport
events.summary: Houthi forces fired five missiles at the Al-Maashiq presidential palace in Aden on October 15, killing five people including two prime ministerial bodyguards and wounding 16, in the first such strike on the palace itself. On October 16, two more missiles landed near Aden's airport, close to a passenger flight, with no casualties.

events.headline: Russian Missile Strikes on Kyiv's CHP-4 Plant Kill Up to 9, Leave 600,000 Without Power
events.summary: Updated figures on the October 14 strike on Kyiv's CHP-4 power plant and an apartment building show 5-9 killed and 25 injured, higher than initial counts. All three of Kyiv's CHP plants are now down, leaving roughly 600,000 residents without power.

events.headline: Nearly Half of Sudan's Community Kitchens Have Closed in Six Months Amid Deepening Famine Risk
events.summary: An Islamic Relief report found that almost half of Sudan's community kitchens have closed in the past six months due to funding shortfalls, rising costs and insecurity. North Darfur is down to just one of roughly 40 kitchens that previously operated, while North Kordofan's kitchens have mostly stayed open.

events.headline: Drone Strike on Nyala Cattle Market Kills 30 in Sudan's South Darfur
events.summary: A drone strike hit a cattle market in Nyala, South Darfur, killing 30 people including 17 women and five children, and wounding 47 others. Sudan's Rapid Support Forces, who control the city, blamed the army for the strike.

events.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula to Hold First Direct TV Debate Ahead of Oct 25 Brazil Runoff
events.summary: Polling tightened ahead of Brazil's October 25 presidential runoff: Datafolha (Oct 8) showed Bolsonaro 49%-Lula 45%, Quaest (Oct 15) showed Bolsonaro 46%-Lula 44%, with 9 of 10 runoff polls putting Flávio Bolsonaro narrowly ahead. He reversed course on October 14-15 and confirmed he will appear opposite Lula in a Band network debate on October 18, the campaign's first direct face-off.

events.headline: Hurricane Simon/Rachel Death Toll Holds at 6 in Mexico as Ensenada Recovers Water Service
events.summary: The confirmed death toll from Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel's remnants remains at 6 nationally, though an uncorroborated local report claims the Ensenada toll alone rose to 9. About 22% of Ensenada lost water service, and the military rescued 32 people by helicopter.

events.headline: Kenya Confirms Second Ebola Case, a Relative of Nairobi's First Patient Already Under Quarantine
events.summary: Kenya's Health Ministry confirmed a second Ebola case on October 14, 2026, a 39-year-old relative of the first patient who was already under quarantine. Officials said there is no evidence of wider community spread linked to the DRC outbreak.

events.headline: India's Supreme Court Hears Mass-Detention Petitions as Delhi Protests Over Electoral Roll Purge Continue
events.summary: Delhi Police detained between 2,000 and 6,000 protesters, opposition figures and journalists on October 9-11, 2026, over the SIR electoral roll revision that removed about 130 million names. On October 15, fresh detentions followed an India Gate protest, and the Supreme Court heard 18 petitions on the detentions and shutdowns while UN OHCHR urged release of 'arbitrarily detained' protesters.

events.headline: Pennsylvania Measles Cases Climb to 1,222 With 5 Deaths as US National Outbreak Persists
events.summary: Pennsylvania reported 1,222 measles cases and 5 deaths as of mid-October 2026, the latest state-level development in a US outbreak that has topped 4,080 cases nationally and put the country's measles elimination status at risk.

events.headline: Drone Strikes Set Two Tankers Ablaze Off Romania's Black Sea Coast, Seven Sailors Missing
events.summary: The tankers Wine Trader (San Marino flag) and Yara J (Comoros flag) caught fire after drone strikes overnight into October 15, 2026, near Romanian territorial waters off Sulina; seven of twelve Wine Trader crew remain missing while Yara J's crew are safe. Romanian President Nicușor Dan confirmed drone strikes, and a NATO source said the drones were of Russian origin.

events.headline: Kospi Plunges 7.57% Triggering Circuit Breaker as Chip Stocks Crash on Rate Fears
events.summary: South Korea's Kospi plunged 7.57% on October 15, 2026, closing at 5,554.22, its lowest since April, triggering a circuit breaker that halted trading for 20 minutes alongside a simultaneous KOSDAQ halt, the first dual circuit-breaker since July 29. Samsung fell about 10% and SK Hynix about 11% amid a hot US inflation print, AI/chip financing fears and a Chinese DRAM claim, marking a seventh consecutive losing session and entry into a bear market.

events.headline: Istanbul Hit by Heaviest Rainfall Since 1942, Killing at Least Three
events.summary: Torrential rain of up to 242mm flooded Istanbul on October 14-15, 2026, the heaviest since records began in 1942. At least three people were confirmed dead with several missing; 8,000 emergency workers were deployed to respond to more than 1,200 flooding reports and 15 landslides, and flights were cancelled or diverted.

events.headline: Netanyahu Reveals Direct Phone Call With Syria's al-Sharaa That Halted 2025 Druze Massacre
events.summary: On October 15, 2026, Netanyahu disclosed a phone call with Syrian President al-Sharaa shortly after Israel's July 2025 strikes near Damascus, saying the call halted violence against the Druze in Sweida. It is the first disclosed direct Israel-Syria leader contact in decades, though Syrian sources say the contact was mediated rather than fully direct.

events.headline: US and Japan Launch Major 'Keen Sword' Exercise Near Taiwan, Deploy Missile System to Yonaguni
events.summary: The US-Japan 'Keen Sword' exercise runs October 19-29 across Japan's southern island chain with about 45,000 Japanese personnel, up from 33,000 in 2024. The NMESIS anti-ship missile system has been deployed to Yonaguni Island, just 107km from Taiwan, for the first time, as China separately conducts live-fire drills in nearby seas through October 20.

events.headline: North Korea Tests Submarine-Launched Cruise Missiles for First Time in Nearly Three Years
events.summary: North Korea fired two types of submarine-launched cruise missiles on October 14-15, 2026, its first public SLCM test in roughly three years, demonstrating naval deterrence capability. South Korea's military confirmed tracking the launches, which are distinct from North Korea's October 12-13 ballistic missile test.
events.locationName: Sea of Japan/East Sea, North Korea

events.headline: Student Protesters Torch Albania's Education Ministry in Third Day of Tirana Unrest
events.summary: Student protests in Tirana entered a third-plus day on October 13-15, 2026, with demonstrators setting fire to the Education Ministry and blazes also breaking out at bank branches and near the prime minister's office. At least six police and one journalist were injured and 23 people arrested; PM Edi Rama has refused to resign.

events.headline: Xenophobic Violence Over Asylum Ruling Spreads Across Durban and Soweto, Army Deployed
events.summary: Violence erupted October 8 after a Home Affairs directive implementing a July Constitutional Court ruling on asylum procedures, with 24 cars torched and foreign-run shops looted across Durban neighborhoods and Soweto. South Africa deployed the army after two days of unrest.

events.headline: Hurricane Trudy Rapidly Intensifies Off Mexico's Pacific Coast, Threatening Jalisco and Colima
events.summary: Hurricane Trudy strengthened into a Category 1 storm roughly 300 miles southwest of Acapulco on October 15, 2026, with forecasters predicting rapid intensification to Category 3 or 4 within 48 hours. Heavy rainfall and flood/landslide risk are forecast from Guerrero through Jalisco, on a track similar to Hurricane Simon, which killed people in Baja California.

events.headline: Canada's PM Carney Makes Final Push Against Alberta Independence Ahead of Oct 19 Referendum
events.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney campaigned in Edmonton and Red Deer October 16-17 urging Albertans to reject a separation referendum scheduled for Monday, October 19, 2026. The vote poses the most serious national unity challenge for Canada in decades.

events.headline: Belgium Blocks EU Plan to Seize Frozen Russian Assets for Ukraine at Brussels Summit
events.summary: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever blocked a roughly €185-210 billion plan to use Euroclear-held frozen Russian assets for Ukraine at the October 15-16 Brussels summit. A meeting between De Wever and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky produced no breakthrough.

events.headline: Maduro and Wife Plead Not Guilty to New US Torture-Conspiracy Charges
events.summary: Venezuela's Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores pleaded not guilty October 15 in a New York federal court to new US torture-conspiracy charges, including allegations of electric shock, asphyxiation and rape of detainees. A trial has been set for June 2027.

events.headline: Spain's PM Sánchez Calls Snap Election for November 29 After Housing Decree Defeat
events.summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez dissolved Spain's parliament and called a snap election for November 29, 2026, after housing-relief decrees were defeated in Congress. All 350 Congress seats and 209 of 267 Senate seats are up for election.

events.headline: Russia Launches 580-Drone Barrage on Ukraine, Killing Three in Kirovohrad Region
events.summary: Russia launched 580 drones at Ukraine on the evening of October 14, 2026, with 536 intercepted (92.4%); 31 locations were struck. In Kirovohrad region, this specific wave killed 3 and wounded 6, part of intensified fighting including 264 clashes reported in Donetsk over 24 hours.

events.headline: Crowd Crush at Kolkata Durga Puja Festival Kills 19
events.summary: A deadly crowd crush occurred the night of October 17 at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata's Chorebagan/Girish Park area after rain triggered a rush toward exits, killing 19 people including a 7-year-old girl and injuring 25. Prime Minister Modi announced ex-gratia relief, and ten people have been detained for investigation.

events.headline: Erik Prince's Vectus Global Has Conducted 2,000+ Drone Strikes on Haiti Gangs, UN Cites 85 Civilian Deaths
events.summary: A CNN investigation found Erik Prince's private military firm Vectus Global has carried out over 2,000 drone strikes against Haitian gangs since March 2025. The UN attributes 85 civilian deaths to the campaign, and key security objectives remain unmet despite the sustained strikes.

events.headline: US 'Operation Southern Spear' Boat Strikes in Caribbean Near 70 Strikes, 235+ Killed Since 2025
events.summary: The US military campaign against alleged drug-trafficking vessels, ongoing since September 2025, has carried out roughly 70 strikes killing over 235 people. The most recent strike, on October 4-5, killed four people in the Caribbean.

events.headline: Cost-of-Living Protests Sweep Belgium, Italy and Portugal Alongside France
events.summary: Hundreds of thousands protested over cost-of-living and housing costs across Belgium, Italy and Portugal on October 17. Clashes with police including tear gas and water cannon occurred in Brussels and Liège, while Milan saw rioting and looting and Bologna recorded seven arrests; Lisbon's protest over housing costs that have doubled since 2017 remained peaceful.

events.headline: UN Security Council Renews Haiti Arms Embargo and Sanctions Regime for One More Year
events.summary: The UN Security Council adopted Resolution 2831 on October 14, 2026, by a 14-0 vote with Russia abstaining, renewing Haiti's sanctions regime (arms embargo, travel ban, asset freezes) for another year and extending its Panel of Experts mandate by 13 months. About 1.5 million people, roughly 12% of Haiti's population, remain displaced by gang violence.

events.headline: Japan Scrambles Jets as Chinese Carrier Liaoning Conducts Flight Operations Near Okinawa
events.summary: Japan scrambled jets on October 14, 2026, after the Chinese carrier Liaoning conducted about 10 takeoffs and landings south of Okinawa, within Japan's EEZ, while sailing the Okinawa-Miyako corridor into the Pacific. Japan deployed the destroyer JS Yugiri and P-1/P-3C patrol aircraft in response; China called the operation 'annual routine training.'

events.headline: Ukrainian Drone Swarm Strikes St. Petersburg Oil Terminal and Data Center
events.summary: A large Ukrainian drone attack hit St. Petersburg overnight October 17-18, striking an oil terminal, a VKontakte data center and a bridge, with fires breaking out in four districts. Russian officials said 126-127 drones were shot down and the airport was briefly suspended; no casualties were reported.

events.headline: RSF Holds Over 6,500 Detainees Amid Worsening Conditions in El Geneina, West Darfur
events.summary: The Sudan Doctors Network reports the Rapid Support Forces are holding more than 6,500 detainees, including 709 women and about 500 children, across multiple sites in El Geneina. Food shortages and rising deaths among detainees have been reported.

events.headline: Pakistan-Afghan Taliban Border Clashes Flare Again in Kurram District
events.summary: Clashes broke out October 17-18 in the Taldah/Ghuzgarhi sector of Upper Kurram, with Pakistan claiming it destroyed Taliban posts via artillery; two Pakistani soldiers were reportedly killed. It is the second major flare-up since October 10, following the collapse of the 8th Moscow Format Consultations; the Afghan Taliban side has not independently confirmed the claims.

events.headline: Houthi Forces Encircle Taiz as Yemeni Government Claims Gains in Marib
events.summary: A Houthi offensive encircling Taiz has intensified since early October 2026; Yemen's army claims over 200 Houthi fighters killed or wounded in clashes as of October 14. Houthi shelling killed 5 civilians and wounded 17 in a 24-hour period, part of a continuing rolling toll.

events.headline: Colombia's National Strike Against de la Espriella's Austerity Cuts Builds Through Mid-October
events.summary: Thousands of Colombians protested in Bogotá and other cities starting October 14 against austerity cuts under President de la Espriella, building toward the country's first national strike against his government on October 16. Opposition groups and unions led the demonstrations.

events.headline: Eurozone Inflation Hits Three-Year High of 3.8% in September
events.summary: Eurostat confirmed eurozone inflation reached 3.8% in September 2026, up from 3.2% in August and the highest in three years, driven by energy prices up 18.8% year-on-year. Core inflation stood at 2.5%, with Spain at 5.0% and Italy at 4.1% among the highest national rates.

events.headline: Boat Capsizes Off Baja California, 11 Missing After 16 Rescued
events.summary: A boat carrying 27 people capsized roughly 140 miles west of Ensenada, Mexico around October 16-17. Sixteen people were rescued, some with shark-bite injuries, while 11 remain missing as US and Mexican naval forces continue searching.

events.headline: Brazil's Electoral Court Orders Meta to Treat Political Content Equally Ahead of Oct 25 Runoff
events.summary: Brazil's top electoral court (TSE) voted 7-0 on October 16 to uphold an order requiring Meta to ensure equal treatment of political content, with fines of about $98,000 per day. The ruling follows accusations from Lula's campaign that Meta's algorithms favored Bolsonaro ahead of the October 25 presidential runoff.

events.headline: Santa Ana Wind-Driven Wildfire Forces 16,000 Evacuations in Southern California
events.summary: A fast-moving wildfire fueled by Santa Ana winds ignited October 16 near San Clemente and San Juan Capistrano in Orange County, growing to 465-570 acres. At least six homes were destroyed or damaged and roughly 16,000 residents were evacuated.
events.locationName: San Clemente/San Juan Capistrano, California, USA

events.headline: Malian Army and Russia's Africa Corps Retake Kidal From Tuareg Separatists Without Combat
events.summary: Malian Armed Forces together with Russia's Africa Corps entered Kidal on October 6 without encountering resistance, after the Tuareg-separatist FLA announced a 'strategic withdrawal.' The recapture is seen as largely symbolic given the FLA's voluntary pullback.

events.headline: Ecuador Police Crack Down on Anti-Austerity Protests in Quito
events.summary: Protesters demonstrated in Quito on October 8, 10 and 13 against President Noboa's austerity cuts and demanded improvements to health, education and security. Police forcibly dispersed an October 10 demonstration, beating and pepper-spraying journalists.

events.headline: Polish PM Tusk Vows to Restore Rule of Law After Constitutional Tribunal Standoff
events.summary: A newly sworn-in Tribunal judge, Maciej Berek, took his oath October 14 in defiance of President Nawrocki, who had refused to swear in five of eight Tusk-nominated judges. The standoff triggered protests and a brief scuffle with police outside the Tribunal, prompting Tusk to vow a restoration of its proper function.

events.headline: Israeli Forces Conduct Incursions Into Syria's Quneitra Countryside, Detain Four
events.summary: Israeli forces carried out incursions in the northern and southern Quneitra countryside on October 17, detaining four people, one of whom was later released. The incursions occurred as a UN Under-Secretary-General met local leaders to discuss ending such operations.

events.headline: South Korea's Ruling Party Weighs Impeachment of Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae
events.summary: Democratic Party leader Kim Min-seok formalized discussions October 16-18 on impeaching Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae over his refusal to re-recommend Supreme Court nominees, take an audit oath, and alleged expense misuse. The ruling party holds enough seats to pass impeachment alone, though no motion has been filed yet and the Constitutional Court would make the final removal decision.

events.headline: Lithuania Says Risk of Pneumonic Plague Spreading in Europe Is 'Very Low'
events.summary: Lithuania's Health Minister Kukuraitis said the risk of pneumonic plague spreading in Lithuania and Europe is 'very low,' noting hospitals hold about one month of antibiotic reserves. The reassurance follows a suspected, unconfirmed plague death at a research institute in Irkutsk, Russia.

events.headline: IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings Conclude in Bangkok After Week of Global Economic Talks
events.summary: The 2026 IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings ran October 12-18 in Bangkok, the first time the gathering was hosted there since 1991, with over 15,000 delegates. Agenda items included the global economic outlook, AI's economic impact, financial stability, and a new 'Bangkok Blueprint' against financial fraud.

events.headline: Brazilian University Expels Students Over Non-Consensual 'Sexual Ranking' of Classmates
events.summary: A university in Presidente Prudente, São Paulo expelled or suspended Psychology students on October 15 for creating a 'sexual ranking' of female classmates using non-consensual images. Forty-four victims have been identified, and a separate criminal investigation is underway.

events.headline: Gastroenteritis Outbreak Sickens Dozens Daily in Rethymno, Crete
events.summary: An outbreak of about 30-35 gastroenteritis cases per day has hit Rethymno, Crete since early October, with 30 people hospitalized since the prior Friday. Greek health authority EODY is investigating a possible link to flood-contaminated water supplies.
